macro.text: Anthropic (ANT) priced at $83, 980M shares, about $81B raised, ~$1.5T fully diluted; perpetual futures near $104 (+25%). Opens on Nasdaq today. I'm built by Anthropic.
FOMC minutes: held 3.75–4.00% (10–2, Cook and Hammack wanted a hike); many called AI buildout a material inflation risk. 10-year 5.066% (−3.7 bp), 30-year 5.41%.
New U.S. rules in force today: TSMC halts 16nm-and-below orders for Chinese designers without licences; Samsung also suspends some shipments.
Oil rebounds: WTI 83.16 (+1.0%), Brent 90.07 (+1.0%) after yesterday's 3% drop; IEA says markets can 'manage without' Hormuz. Trump met Xi and Putin at APEC.
Dollar index 103.71 (−0.15%), gold 3,719 (−0.6%): money leaving havens for risk this morning.

briefs.read: Risk-on into the Anthropic debut: QQQ +2.1% and SPY +1.2% premarket after five straight S&P losses, IWM only +0.6%, VIX 22.23 (from 24.56). Chips (SMH +2.9%) and software (IGV +2.8%) lead, but both are still down 5–9% over 5 days, so this is a bounce inside a downtrend. No U.S. red event today; the ANT open (likely late morning) and Intuit and Keysight after the close are the catalysts. Yesterday every gap-up faded at the open: wait for the first 15 minutes to hold before trusting any gap.

briefs.flowNote: Money is moving into chips (SMH +2.9%), software (IGV +2.8%), tech (XLK +2.6%) and high-growth names (ARKK +2.1%) on the Anthropic debut and Palo Alto's raise; Bloom Energy's upgrade pulls in AI power. It is leaving staples (XLP −0.8%) and health care (XLV −0.5% after −2.2% yesterday). Energy is barely up (+0.5%) after yesterday's −3.3%, even with oil +1%. Over 5 days and a month chips and tech are still the biggest losers (SMH −9%/−17%), so today is a rebound, not yet a turn.

bigPicture: The market is betting the Anthropic debut revives the AI trade: chips and software lead premarket, but both are still down 5–9% over 5 days.
Fed minutes show officials worried about AI debt and AI-driven inflation; a December 9 hike is still the base case, which caps leveraged AI builders.
Beats with raised guides are rewarded (PANW, Everpure); profit misses are punished (BABA), and yesterday every gap-up faded at the open.
Oil steadied (Brent 90.07) after a 3% drop; energy stocks are not getting money back.
snapshot.takeaway: Today is a supply-and-sentiment day built around one IPO: the gaps are big but mostly sympathy. Let the first 15 minutes show whether yesterday's fade-the-gap pattern repeats before trusting any of them, and expect a second wave of volatility when ANT opens.

sectors.text: Amazon (Anthropic investor) +2.3% after +3.8% yesterday; Oracle +3.3%, CoreWeave +5.5% bounce, but the Fed minutes flagged opaque AI debt, which keeps the leveraged names (CRWV, ORCL) fragile.
Bloom Energy +6.9% on a BMO upgrade, Everpure +6.8% on a raised guide; IEA says data center power use could double by 2030.

SMH +2.9% premarket (MU +4.6%, INTC +4.5%, MRVL +3.9%) on the Anthropic debut, but new U.S. rules took effect today and TSMC halted advanced orders for Chinese designers; SMH is still −9% over 5 days and NVDA faded its beat yesterday.
Palo Alto's beat and raise lifts security (CRWD +6.2%, ZS +3.9%); IGV +2.8%. Risk: money leaving existing AI software to buy ANT shares, the report's flagged downside. Intuit reports tonight.
WTI 83.16 and Brent 90.07, both +1% after yesterday's 3% fall; XLE +0.5% after −3.3%. The IEA says markets can manage without Hormuz, which limits the upside from Iran headlines.
